candidates.label: Acute ophthalmic artery occlusion (right eye) with secondary angle-closure glaucoma
Central retinal artery occlusion (right eye) with cilioretinal artery sparing
missing_or_uncertain: choroidal involvement not typical for CRAO

candidates.label: Acute angle-closure glaucoma with ischemic retinopathy (right eye)
Orbital compartment syndrome (right eye) due to spontaneous retrobulbar hemorrhage
Purtscher retinopathy (right eye) secondary to rhabdomyolysis

response.rationale: The acute painless vision loss with no light perception, high IOP, and fluorescein angiography showing delayed choroidal filling and poor perfusion strongly indicate ophthalmic artery occlusion, which affects both retinal and choroidal circulations. The systemic rhabdomyolysis and acute kidney injury are likely coincidental or related to alcohol/drug use, but the eye findings are most consistent with OAO. CRAO is less likely due to choroidal involvement, and other diagnoses are poorly supported by the imaging findings.
